reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a tutorial for requesting a withdrawal from an Argent Global Network wallet, including the stated minimum withdrawal and payment-account steps. It instructs account holders to submit identity and address documents for verification, but the observable material does not establish a deceptive promise, fraudulent destination, or request to send money to the creator. The description also mentions crowdfunding a OneCoin presentation, although that solicitation is not developed in the supplied withdrawal tutorial.

citations.quote: I've gotten a lot of questions recently about how to withdraw your money from your wallet. So I am here to do a little video about how to do just that
go to your dashboard and go to transfer funds
you can only request withdrawal on Mondays
minimum withdrawal should be $40

So in order for you to confirm your identification and address you had to upload some kind of document. What you can upload is just something like passport or driver's license or anything like that that shows your full name and your photo and also your date of birth and your address.

opening.argument: Judge the withdrawal promise together with the action required to claim it. The video tells viewers they can request money from their wallet, but only through a Monday withdrawal window and after supplying identity documents. The accompanying member update makes the dependency sharper: members are told to send identification and proof of address by email, and that only verified members will be allowed to withdraw in the coming weeks. This is not merely information about money; it directs viewers seeking a payout to hand over sensitive documents as the condition for accessing it.

citations.quote: you can only request withdrawal on Mondays
So in order for you to confirm your identification and address you had to upload some kind of document.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls this a dashboard tutorial, but that describes the format, not the effect of the instructions. Its cited verification requirement is precisely the concern: access to a withdrawal is tied to submitting identity and address records. Nor does the absence of a request to pay the creator resolve a case centered on obtaining sensitive documents. The member update explicitly directs their submission by email before withdrawals are allowed.

citations.quote: So in order for you to confirm your identification and address you had to upload some kind of document.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The argument identifies a real verification requirement but does not show that the withdrawal is a free or unusually easy reward, or that verification is deceptive. The speaker describes withdrawing money already in the viewer's wallet and explains the dashboard procedure. The member update likewise frames document submission as verification; its presence does not establish misuse of those documents or a fraudulent payout.

citations.quote: how to withdraw your money from your wallet
go to your dashboard and go to transfer funds

opening.argument: Several warning signs converge around the promised withdrawal. Viewers are given a narrow Monday-only request window, a $40 minimum, and requirements for documents bearing a name, photograph, birth date, address and document number. The form also asks for a payment-account destination and an identity-card number. Taken together, these conditions make the prospect of receiving money a strong inducement to provide both account identifiers and unusually detailed personal information. The video demonstrates how to comply, but provides no evidence that completing these steps actually produces a withdrawal.

citations.quote: you can only request withdrawal on Mondays
minimum withdrawal should be $40
your full name and your photo and also your date of birth and your address. And this document should also have a document number.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense relies on the absence of an explicit fraudulent promise. But its own description leaves the central outcome unverified: the speaker says users should be able to request withdrawals, not that a payout is shown. The Monday restriction, minimum amount and detailed identity requirements matter in combination because they make viewers act under conditions set by the wallet before any receipt of money is demonstrated.

citations.quote: you should be able to do this every monday
minimum withdrawal should be $40

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Those conditions warrant attention, but none establishes deception. A minimum, a request schedule and identity checks can be ordinary withdrawal rules. The speaker says the money is already in the user's wallet, then walks through the withdrawal form; this is not a claim of effortless new income. A tutorial's failure to show a completed payout does not itself show that payouts fail.

And Account which one of these you want your money to go to

opening.argument: The tutorial framing should not obscure where it steers viewers. It walks an existing account holder from the dashboard to a withdrawal request, tells them which payment-account identifiers to enter, and ends with agreement and submission. The description also appeals for crowdfunding for a new OneCoin USA presentation. In that context, the video does more than neutrally define a withdrawal term: it encourages continued engagement with an account system by presenting a concrete route to getting money out, while leaving the actual payout unshown.

click this check mark right here input withdrawal
OneCoin Team USA WE NEED YOUR HELP - BIG News - We are Crowdfunding a New OneCoin USA presentation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the crowdfunding line as separate because the spoken tutorial does not develop it. Yet it is part of the supplied description, and the tutorial itself repeatedly guides viewers toward completing the wallet's process. Calling that guidance operational does not settle whether the prospect of withdrawing money is being used to sustain participation. The cited steps establish a pathway to a request, not a completed payment.

citations.quote: We are Crowdfunding a New OneCoin USA presentation.
go to your dashboard and go to transfer funds
you should be able to do this every monday

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The description's crowdfunding appeal is real, but nothing in the spoken withdrawal instructions connects a donation to receiving money. The speaker addresses people who already have a wallet and explains where to request a withdrawal and which existing payment account to select. Reframing practical instructions as promotion does not supply a deceptive reward claim or show that viewers must pay or recruit anyone to withdraw.
